findings.text: Shared acquisition entry points that may sleep until read ownership is granted. Uninterruptible interruptible and killable wait flavours exist with interruption reported as failure and dependency state released on failure. Nested forms accept a subclass for dependency tracking. A fast nonblocking attempt precedes entry to the blocking path.

Non owner read handling where acquisition and release are decoupled from recorded owner identity. Acquisition performs the normal shared wait then clears the reader owned marker to a null holder. Release asserts reader owned state then performs the normal shared release without requiring current ownership.

Exclusive acquisition entry points that may sleep until write ownership is granted. Killable waiting reports interruption as failure with dependency state released. Nested forms accept either a subclass number or a nest dependency object for correct ordering. A fast nonblocking attempt precedes the blocking path.

Nonblocking attempts to obtain shared or exclusive ownership that never sleep. Success is indicated by a positive result and records dependency acquisition as a try. Failure leaves the caller without ownership and without dependency state.

Conversion of current exclusive ownership to shared ownership while retaining holdership. Dependency state is moved from exclusive to shared before the internal conversion runs so a waiting reader set can be granted without fully releasing the semaphore.

Counting semaphore acquisition entry points plus a holder query. The blocking forms sleep uninterruptibly or interruptibly until a unit becomes available with interruption reported as failure. A separate query returns an opaque holder cookie for hung task diagnosis with one build tracking the last holder and another build always reporting zero.

Reader owned spinning uses a deadline derived from current scheduler time plus a delay that grows with observed reader count. The reader count contribution is capped at thirty and the delay scales a microsecond unit by a base of twenty plus reader count then halved. Callers sample the clock sparingly and compare against this deadline to decide when to stop spinning.

Writer optimistic spinning first secures a queuing slot then repeatedly observes the owner condition. Nonspinnable observation ends the attempt. Each observation is followed by an unqueued exclusive attempt that on success ends spinning as taken. Reader owned observation starts a time bounded window on first entry and about every sixteenth iteration checks expiry to mark nonspinnable. Scheduling need and real time constraints abort spinning when the owner is not a running writer with prior owner state retained across iterations. The queuing slot is always released and failure is accounted.

An alternate build disables owner based spinning entirely. Eligibility always reports false owner observation always reports nonspinnable and the optimistic attempt always reports failure without waiting or acquiring.

Wake selection under the wait lock examines the count word. Presence of writer related bits suppresses waking. Presence of reader related bits requests a reader wake. Otherwise any waiter may be woken and the nonspinnable mark is cleared to re allow spinning. Selection is then handed to the wake marking helper with a batched wake queue.

Reader slowpath balances stealing against fairness and sleeping. It refuses stealing when reader ownership with multiple readers and no writer lock suggests writer starvation risk. It allows stealing when neither writer locked nor handoff is set marking reader owned and waking queued readers when the caller is the first reader and waiters exist. Otherwise it enqueues the caller adjusts the count to drop speculative bias and possibly set the waiter flag evaluates conditional waking then sleeps in the requested state until ownership is granted or a pending signal aborts with queue removal and error propagation.

Writer slowpath first tries the optimistic path when allowed returning immediately on success with acquire ordering. On failure it enqueues the caller and ensures the waiter flag is set issuing conditional waking for existing queues with minimal lock hold time. The caller then loops attempting acquisition under the wait lock sleeping outside the lock between attempts. After handoff is set a null owner observation causes an immediate retry without sleeping. Pending signals abort with queue removal and error propagation while success clears blocker state and restores running state.

Downgrade wake takes the wait lock with interrupts saved and when a first waiter exists requests a read owned wake into a batched queue. The lock is released before delivering the batched wakes keeping wake delivery outside the spin protected region.

Shared acquisition wrappers share a common helper that disables preemption across the attempt. The helper tries a fast nonblocking acquisition and on failure enters the reader slowpath in the requested sleep state converting slowpath failure into an interrupt error. Uninterruptible interruptible and killable wrappers differ only in the sleep state passed through and preemption is re enabled before returning.

Internal shared trylock validates the semaphore identity disables preemption and repeatedly compares the count word against a failure mask. When clear it attempts an atomic compare exchange adding one reader bias with acquire ordering. Success marks reader owned state and reports positive otherwise preemption is restored and failure is reported without sleeping.

Exclusive acquisition wrappers share a common helper that disables preemption across the attempt. The helper tries a fast exclusive acquisition and on failure enters the writer slowpath in the requested sleep state converting slowpath failure into an interrupt error. Uninterruptible and killable wrappers differ only in sleep state while the internal trylock wrapper validates identity and returns the fast result directly. Preemption is re enabled before returning.

Internal downgrade requires current exclusive ownership disables preemption and atomically replaces the writer locked contribution with one reader bias using release ordering so prior exclusive region effects do not leak into the read side. It then marks reader owned state and when the prior count indicated waiters records contention and invokes the downgrade wake helper before re enabling preemption.
Presence of a build selector macro indicating the real time mutex based construction variant of this translation unit.

Initialization entry for the real time variant that initializes the embedded read write base object and when lock allocation debugging is enabled validates that no locks are being freed over this memory and initializes the dependency map for sleeping waits.

Real time variant shared operations that delegate directly to the embedded read write base object. Blocking forms forward the caller sleep state for uninterruptible interruptible and killable waits while the trylock form forwards a nonblocking attempt without sleep state.

Real time variant exclusive operations that delegate directly to the embedded read write base object. Blocking forms forward uninterruptible or killable sleep states the trylock form forwards a nonblocking attempt and downgrade forwards conversion from exclusive to shared.

Semaphore unit acquisition decrements the count and records the current holder for diagnosis when that tracking build is active. Holder clearing only clears when the current task matches the recorded holder. An alternate build provides empty tracking operations so acquisition only affects the count.

Semaphore waiting links the caller record at the queue tail or as the sole head then sleeps with timeout handling. Interruption and expiry each remove the record and report distinct errors while a grant flag set by the waker ends the wait with holder recording and success. Removal handles empty list sole head and interior cases by updating the first waiter pointer and unlinking as needed.

Semaphore blocking wrappers share helpers that mark the caller as blocked on the semaphore for hung task diagnosis bracket the wait with contention tracing and clear the blocker mark on exit. Uninterruptible and interruptible forms differ only in sleep state and both use an unbounded timeout.

Signal and timeout exits must remove the waiter from the queue under wait protection and propagate a wake to a successor when required otherwise a stale record or lost wake can stall later acquirers. Callers distinguish success from interruption or expiry by distinct error results and must not assume ownership on failure.

Fast try paths run with preemption disabled and never sleep while slow paths sleep only after releasing spin protection and with interrupts restored appropriately. Wait lock acquisition uses interrupt disabling or saving forms and wake delivery is batched for release outside the lock to bound hold time and avoid sleeping while spin held.

Fragments access waiter and control records through named members rather than showing complete type definitions. Reader writer waiter use shows task identity wait kind timeout instant handoff flag and list linkage plus a first waiter head. Semaphore waiter use shows task identity grant flag and list linkage plus a first waiter head and integer count with spin protection.

Semaphore acquisition holds the protecting spinlock with interrupts saved across the count test. Positive count takes a unit inline and releases the lock. Nonpositive count enters the blocking wait while still holding the lock on entry to the wait helper with unlock and relock paired around each schedule.
